statusDetail: Coverage-complete public, unauthenticated audit across landing, listing, live schedule, sign-in, and error archetypes. Credentialed playback, purchase, cancellation, and account management were not exercised.

page.notes: Root redirects to a UK non-Prime landing. Public pages are server-rendered and progressively enhanced; account authentication is hosted on amazon.co.uk.

paths.description: Root/UK non-Prime landing: entry, offer clarity, consent, global metadata/security/performance, desktop/mobile/preferences.
Movies listing archetype: navigation state, media feed, consent, narrow layout, repeated scrolling/memory.
Live TV schedule archetype: category navigation, schedule density, locale/time presentation, narrow layout.
Primary public conversion/auth hand-off: sign-in form, labels/autocomplete, empty submission, mobile layout.
Network/HTTP failure recovery using a nonexistent public route.

findings.summary: The cookie notice obscures most of the primary content on every public browse surface.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots show a 398px-tall overlay covering the hero and listings; on the 360px capture it occupies the bottom quarter while the page is scaled down.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent surface for optional cookies, retain equally prominent Accept and Decline actions, and reserve a modal only when interaction must truly stop.

findings.summary: The blocking cookie overlay is not exposed as a dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found no dialog element, role=dialog, or aria-modal while the visible overlay blocks and visually dominates the page.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the blocking surface with <dialog>, an accessible name, controlled focus, Escape handling, and predictable focus restoration.

findings.summary: Public and sign-in pages omit the viewport meta tag, so mobile browsers render a 980px layout and scale it down.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport, layout evidence reports clientWidth 980, visual scale 0.367, and hasViewportMeta=false on home, movie, live TV, and sign-in.
findings.suggestedFix: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> and verify reflow at 320-400 CSS px without disabling user zoom.

findings.summary: The landing experience uses a fixed dark palette rather than adapting to color-scheme and contrast preferences.
findings.evidence: Normal, prefers-color-scheme:dark, and prefers-contrast:more screenshots are pixel-identical; DOM/CSS searches found no prefers-color-scheme, prefers-contrast, or forced-colors rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and define preference-driven tokens with prefers-color-scheme plus forced-colors/prefers-contrast overrides for essential controls.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-only; no container-query rules were found for reusable navigation, hero, or schedule components.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM/CSS evidence across home, movie, and live TV contains no @container or container-type declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards, navigation groups, and schedule rows containment and adapt them with size container queries while retaining a viewport fallback.

findings.summary: Cold, throttled loading is slow despite a fast unthrottled trace.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse performance is 0.55 with FCP 10.2s, LCP 15.7s, and TTI 15.7s; the unthrottled trace corroborates low blocking work but not the network-constrained experience.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP request chain under mobile throttling, preload only the selected LCP asset, reduce redirects and render-blocking dependencies, and retest field-like conditions.

findings.summary: Large render-blocking chains and substantial unused code delay first render.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 6.46s render-blocking savings, 601KiB unused JavaScript, 103KiB unused CSS, and 94KiB legacy JavaScript; HAR confirms parser-inserted very-high-priority stylesheets and high-priority scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Split route and widget bundles, remove legacy/duplicate code, inline only critical CSS, defer non-critical scripts, and shorten the parser-blocking dependency chain.

findings.summary: The page has no main landmark.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility reports landmark-one-main as the sole failing accessibility audit, and the DOM probe found header, nav, and footer but no main element or role=main.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the unique page content in one <main> landmark and keep repeated navigation outside it.

findings.summary: Several image elements lack dimensions and responsive delivery; some rendered images have no alt text.
findings.evidence: The images primitive reports 3/4 images without width/height, 2 oversized, no modern formats, and 3 without alt; Lighthouse independently flags the visible navigation and footer logos as unsized.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height, use responsive srcset/sizes and modern formats, and give meaningful images an alt value while keeping decorative images explicitly alt="".

findings.summary: Browser security policy and cookie defenses are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows no CSP, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. Cookie evidence finds csm-hit and i18n-prefs without Secure and auth-like session-id/session-token values without HttpOnly, all SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP, explicit Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; mark all HTTPS cookies Secure, restrict SameSite, and make server-only session credentials HttpOnly.

findings.summary: The unauthenticated landing page has a broad telemetry and third-party request footprint before consent choice.
findings.evidence: HAR records 83/104 requests and 6.03MB/6.20MB as third-party by origin classification; tracker evidence lists eight third-party origins including multiple analytics/event endpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate optional telemetry until consent, consolidate and batch essential events, inventory each external origin, and remove calls without direct user value.

findings.summary: Locale and indexing signals conflict on the UK landing experience.
findings.evidence: The rendered page says Amazon.co.uk and redirects UK users, but html lang is en-us and canonical points to /-/en_US/gp/video/offers; /sitemap.xml returned a branded 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit the actual locale in lang, point canonical to the equivalent UK locale URL, add reciprocal hreflang entries, and expose a valid sitemap URL in robots.txt.

findings.summary: The public offer page has social tags but no structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found three Open Graph tags and zero application/ld+json blocks on a public service/offer landing page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate JSON-LD for WebSite/Organization and applicable Offer or VideoObject entities, matching visible content and localized URLs.

findings.summary: Submitting the empty sign-in form gives no visible validation or recovery message.
findings.evidence: After activating Continue with the empty focused email field and waiting 1.5s, the screenshot remains unchanged with no visible error announcement.
findings.suggestedFix: After interaction, identify the required value with visible, specific text, associate it with aria-describedby/aria-invalid, focus or announce the error, and preserve the entered value.

findings.summary: Route and major state changes have no detectable declarative transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The probe reports no active animations and rendered CSS evidence contains no View Transition CSS; navigation changes are abrupt while active tabs merely swap style.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for route and detail changes, with a reduced-motion fallback and motion tied to navigation direction.

findings.summary: Repeated feed traversal retained substantially more heap and objects.
findings.evidence: Heap summaries after ten bottom/top traversals grew from 70.5MB/1,139,190 nodes to 95.5MB/1,524,576 nodes, including Objects 73,053→191,008 and closures 55,828→83,413.
findings.suggestedFix: Run a baseline/target/final heap workflow with explicit GC, identify retainers for loaded cards/listeners, virtualize or evict offscreen feed data, and clean up subscriptions and timers.

findings.summary: The unauthenticated landing transfers disproportionate image and font payloads.
findings.evidence: HAR totals 6.20MB: 3.74MB images and 1.02MB across 29 fonts; one 2880x1350 JPEG alone transfers 3.72MB. The image probe finds no modern formats or responsive source for the audited images.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve an AVIF/WebP responsive hero sized to the viewport, subset and consolidate fonts, lazy-load below-fold media, and enforce route-specific byte budgets.

findings.summary: The prominent Join Prime path does not disclose price or commitment before sending users into account authentication.
findings.evidence: Home and movie screenshots show repeated Join Prime actions and subscription language without a visible price, renewal term, or trial commitment; /signup redirects directly to Amazon Sign-In.
findings.suggestedFix: Place localized price, billing cadence, trial/renewal terms, and a clear cancellation route adjacent to every Join Prime action before authentication.

Cut the critical path and unused route payload
Harden security headers and session cookies
Optimize the hero, fonts, and third-party budget
Make consent compact, semantic, and accessible
Disclose Prime price and renewal terms before authentication
Investigate and bound retained feed memory
Add main landmark and correct image semantics/dimensions
Align UK locale, canonical, hreflang, and sitemap signals
Provide humane sign-in validation and autocomplete
Respect theme/contrast and add component responsiveness
